 \begin{lemma}[Fourier expansion of Pauli observables]\label{lem:pauli-observable-expansion}
 	\uses{def:generalized-pauli, def:subfield-trace}
 	For every integer $n \ge 1$, all $W \in \{X, Z\}$, and all $a \in \F_q^n$,
 	% Paper equation label kept on the display it names.
 	\begin{equation}\label{eq:pauli-obs-proj}
 		\tau^W(a) = \sum_{b \in \F_q^n} \omega^{\tr(a \cdot b)}\, \tau^W_b\;,
 	\end{equation}
 	and conversely
 	\begin{equation}\label{eq:pauli-inversion-0}
 		\E_{\ba \sim \F_q^n}\, \omega^{-\tr(\ba \cdot b)}\, \tau^W(\ba)
 		= \sum_{b' \in \F_q^n} \E_{\ba \sim \F_q^n}\,
 		\omega^{\tr(\ba \cdot (b' - b))}\, \tau^W_{b'}
 		= \tau^W_b\;.
 	\end{equation}
 	The source scope and the binary specialization of these identities are
 	recorded in \cite{gap:qpbt_characteristic-two-pauli-scope}.
 \end{lemma}
 \begin{proof}
 	\uses{def:generalized-pauli, lem:cancellation}
 	Each $\ket{b_W}$ is an eigenvector of $\tau^W(a)$ with eigenvalue
 	$\omega^{\tr(a \cdot b)}$: for $W = Z$ this is immediate from the
 	definition, and for $W = X$ it follows from the single-qudit computation
 	$\tau^X(a)\ket{e_X} = \omega^{\tr(ae)}\ket{e_X}$, applied factor by factor.
 	Expanding $\tau^W(a)$ in the orthonormal eigenbasis
 	$\{\ket{b_W}\}_{b \in \F_q^n}$ gives the first display. For the inversion,
 	substitute the first display and exchange the order of summation; by
 	Lemma~\ref{lem:cancellation} applied with $V = \F_q^n$ (so that
 	$V^\perp = \{0\}$), the inner expectation vanishes unless $b' = b$, where
 	it equals $1$.
 \end{proof}

 projectors are isomorphic to tensor products of qubit EPR states

 \begin{lemma}[Qudit-to-qubit isomorphism]\label{lem:pauli-binary}

 	For all admissible field sizes $q = 2^k$ and integers $L \ge 0$, there
 	exists an isomorphism $\phi : (\C^q)^{\ot L} \to (\C^2)^{\ot Lk}$ such that
 	\begin{equation}\label{eq:epr-q-to-epr-2}
 		\phi \ot \phi\, \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot L}
 		= \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_2}^{\ot Lk}
 	\end{equation}
 	(applying the natural identifications between
 	$(\C^q)^{\ot L} \ot (\C^q)^{\ot L}$ and $(\C^q \ot \C^q)^{\ot L}$, and
 	between $(\C^2)^{\ot Lk} \ot (\C^2)^{\ot Lk}$ and
 	$(\C^2 \ot \C^2)^{\ot Lk}$). Moreover, for all $W \in \{X, Z\}$ and all
 	$u \in \F_q^L$,
 	\begin{equation}\label{eq:pauli-q-to-pauli-2}
 		\tau^W_u = \phi^\dagger\,
 		\Bigl(\bigotimes_{i=1}^L \bigotimes_{j=1}^k
 		\sigma^W_{u_{ij}}\Bigr)\, \phi\;.
 	\end{equation}
 	Here $(u_{ij})_{i,j}$ is the array of $\F_2$ values with
 	$u_i = \sum_j u_{ij} e_j$ for all $i \in \{1, \dots, L\}$, where

 	$\F_2$ of Definition~\ref{def:binary-representation}; and for

    10	Throughout this chapter we work in the setting of
    11	Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-observables}: a projective strategy for the Pauli basis
    12	test game succeeds with probability at least $1-\eps$, and all operators act
    13	relative to the expanded state $\ket{\hat\psi}$ on registers

   320

360	  \item \emph{Projectivity round trip.}  The averaged strategy is a POVM
   361	  strategy even when the given one is projective, while the imported
   362	  theorem, like the present one, takes projective strategies.  The
   363	  intended round trip is: dilate the averaged strategy to a projective one
   364	  (Naimark preserves all product correlations
   365	  $\langle X \ot Y \rangle$ of the given strategy against the dilated
   366	  state --- hence the value of every branch the averaging preserved ---
   367	  but nothing restores the diagonal seed correlations once the averaging
   368	  has been performed); apply form~4; and compress the resulting polynomial
   369	  measurement along the dilation isometry back to a POVM in the required
   370	  measurement class on the original space.  That this compression
   371	  preserves the consistency conclusions must itself be proved; it is
   372	  stated here as an obligation, not established.  (Alternatively, form~4
   373	  may be stated for POVM strategies outright, moving the dilation inside
   374	  the import.)
   375	\end{itemize}
   376	
   377	The combining subtree would then be reread with the direct distribution
   378	and the directly indexed game at dimension $2m+2$: every statement becomes
   379	well defined for all admissible tuples, and the expectation is that the
   380	proofs survive unchanged, because the measurements constructed there are
   381	indexed by the geometric data --- points, lines, and polynomials on them
   382	--- and so constitute a strategy for the directly indexed game outright,
   383	with no fiber averaging.  Verifying, lemma by lemma, that those proofs use
   384	only the laws of the sampled objects and never the conditional linearity
   385	of the sampling is part of this direction's obligations.  This follows the
   386	subtree protocol for a definition-level mismatch: the definition is
   387	corrected at the lowest point rather than each downstream lemma acquiring
   388	a hypothesis.  The transport layer costs one parsing-map definition, the
   389	distribution lemma, the pullback lemma, whichever synchronicity control is
   390	chosen, and the dilation--compression lemma; the first three are an
   391	estimated one to two hundred lines on top of the restated import, with the
   392	blueprint's existing Naimark interface supplying the dilation, while the
   393	synchronicity control is the step whose weight is genuinely uncertain.
   394	The external check that the tensor-code test of arXiv:2111.08131 samples
   395	its axes and subcubes directly has been made against that source: Figure~1
   396	there draws the axis index and the subcube data uniformly and directly,
   397	with no index encoding into $\F_q$.
   398	
   399	\paragraph{Padding the dimension.}
   400	Alternatively, embed the combined polynomial into
   401	$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,\bar m}(\F_q)$ for $\bar m = 4m$, the least power of two
   402	with $\bar m \ge 2m+2$, ignoring the $2m-2$ dummy variables.  Then
   403	$\bar m \mid q$ holds whenever $q \ge 4m$, and the existing game applies at
   404	dimension $\bar m$.  In the complementary regime $m \in \{q/2,\, q\}$ the
   405	conclusion is vacuous: $md \ge q/2$ gives
   406	$\delta_S \ge a(md)^a q^{-b} \ge a\,2^{-a} q^{a-b} \ge a\,2^{-b} \ge 1$
   407	for $a \ge 2$, while the consistency quantities bounded by the theorem never
   408	exceed $1$.  This route stays inside the present definitions but reworks the
   409	sub-line distribution (a fourth coordinate block of dummies), the combining
   410	map, and the wrong-block Schwartz--Zippel analysis, and it moves the
   411	combining lemmas away from their source statements at dimension $2m+2$.
   412	
   413	\paragraph{Unequal index classes.}
   414	One could instead define an index function at dimension $2m+2$ with classes
   415	of sizes $\lfloor q/(2m+2)\rfloor$ and $\lceil q/(2m+2)\rceil$.  The index
   416	is then only approximately uniform, the identification with the external
   417	test fails exactly, and every distributional identity in the sub-line
   418	analysis acquires an error term; this amounts to re-proving the imported
   419	soundness theorem for a perturbed game and is not recommended.
   420	
   421	\section{Comparison with the blueprint}
   422	
   423	The blueprint \cite{MIPStarREBlueprint} keeps the sub-line lemma, the
   424	combined line lemma, and the polynomial-pair lemma in their source-shaped
   425	statements, with no divisibility hypothesis.  Their proofs retain the source
   426	constructions and mark the unresolved obligation at the exact steps: the
   427	first sampling step of the sub-line construction, where $\chi_{2m+2}$ and
   428	the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$ are invoked, and the
   429	instantiation step of the polynomial-pair proof, where $(q,2m+2,d,1)$ is
   430	used as a game parameter tuple.  A chapter remark records the divisibility
   431	arithmetic and cites this note; the final soundness theorem for the Pauli
   432	basis test remains open modulo this obligation.  The blueprint's proof node
   433	for the classical soundness import itself states the source's route --- the
   434	identification with the two-prover tensor-code test and the application of
   435	Theorem~4.7 --- and enumerates the two obligations of
   436	Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations} as open, citing this note for the
   437	detailed comparison and the case arithmetic.  An earlier revision had
   438	instead added the hypothesis $2m+2 \mid q$ to the three lemmas; that was
   439	statement drift in the sense of the proof-gap protocol, since the hypothesis
   440	excludes all admissible $m \ge 2$ and does not appear in the source.
   441	
   442	\section{Conclusion}
   443	
   444	There is a theorem-level gap in the source proof route: the classical low
   445	individual degree game invoked at dimension $2m+2$ is undefined for every
   446	admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$ (and for $(q,m) = (2,1)$), because its
   447	question distribution requires $2m+2 \mid q$ while admissibility supplies
   448	only $m \mid q$.  The cited route therefore does not establish the
   449	polynomial-pair lemma, nor the soundness of the Pauli basis test that
   450	depends on it, beyond $m = 1$ and $q \ge 8$.  Independently of the
   451	divisibility, the import of the classical game's quantum soundness carries
   452	the two open verification obligations of
   453	Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}: the asserted identity with the
   454	two-prover tensor-code test must be replaced by a reduction carrying a
   455	value bound, and the source's instantiation of the auxiliary parameter
   456	violates the theorem's lower bound at the small dimensions listed there.
   457	We do not assert that any conclusion is false: the underlying tensor-code
   458	soundness is insensitive to how the axis index is sampled, and both import
   459	obligations concern verification, not counterexample.  For the divisibility
   460	repair, the recommended candidate direction is direct index sampling ---
   461	restate the imported soundness theorem for the directly indexed game at
   462	arbitrary dimension; prove the distribution and parsing-pullback lemmas;
   463	settle the synchronicity control for de-seeding together with the
   464	dilation--compression round trip, so that the present soundness statement
   465	would follow from the repaired import; and reread the combining subtree
   466	against the directly indexed game --- a direction whose open obligations
   467	are enumerated under the candidate repairs, not an established route, with
   468	dimension padding as the fallback confined to the present game definition.

1	# Mathematical Language Guidelines
     2	
     3	MIPStarRE Lean names and documentation should be written for readers comparing
     4	the formalization with the paper and blueprint.
     5	
     6	This is a project-local supplement to the Mathlib-derived documentation,
     7	naming, and style guides in the lean-conventions skill's `MATHLIB_doc`,
     8	`MATHLIB_naming`, and `MATHLIB_style` references.
     9	
    10	## Scope
    11	
    12	These guidelines apply to:
    13	
    14	- public Lean declaration names and namespace names;
    15	- module docstrings;
    16	- declaration docstrings;
    17	- documentation-visible section comments;
    18	- explanatory comments that describe the mathematical role of a declaration.
    19	- blueprint prose and formalization-support notes;
    20	- issue titles and issue bodies;
    21	- PR titles and PR descriptions.
    22	
    23	## Source of Truth
    24	
    25	Use terminology from the following sources, in this order:
    26	
    27	1. `references/ldt-paper/`
    28	2. `blueprint/src/chapter/`
    29	3. established local conventions in nearby Lean files
    30	
    31	When the paper has a term for the object, use that term. For Section 5, for
    32	example, prefer orthogonalization lemma, truncation function, rounding to
    33	projectors, rank reduction, and completing to measurement.
    34	
    35	## Reference Notation And Terminology
    36	
    37	The notation and terminology of the original reference are the default for
    38	reader-facing mathematical text.  A reader should be able to compare a Lean
    39	docstring, blueprint paragraph, issue, or PR description with the cited source
    40	without first learning a private vocabulary used by the formalization.
    41	
    42	When Lean must use a different name or representation, define the deviation in a
    43	location which future readers can find from the affected statement.  Use the
    44	first applicable location in the following order:
    45	
    46	1. the declaration docstring of the public object whose name or representation
    47	   differs from the paper;
    48	2. the module docstring of the defining Lean file, when the deviation concerns a
    49	   family of declarations in that file;
    50	3. the relevant blueprint paragraph, when the notation appears only in the
    51	   blueprint;
    52	4. a report under `docs/reports/` or `docs/paper-gaps/`, when the deviation is a
    53	   larger discrepancy between the paper, blueprint, and Lean.
    54	
    55	The explanation should say:
    56	
    57	- the notation or term used in the paper;
    58	- the Lean object or name which represents it;
    59	- the mathematical reason for the difference, if there is one;
    60	- the scope in which the replacement should be used.
    61	
    62	A PR description may mention the deviation, but it should not be the only place
    63	where future readers can learn it.
    64	
    65	Formalization-only auxiliary lemmas should be introduced as such.  Their prose
    66	should name the nearby paper equation, theorem, or construction they support,
    67	rather than presenting the auxiliary name as paper terminology.
    68	
    69	## Naming Norm
    70	
    71	Names and prose should describe the mathematical object, hypothesis, or
    72	conclusion. They should not encode the history of how the formalization was
    73	assembled.
    74	
    75	Avoid presenting words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`,
    76	`oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as mathematical terminology unless the cited source
    77	uses them with that meaning. Likewise, avoid implementation-local substitutes
    78	such as `projectivization` or `spectral truncation` when the paper gives a
    79	clearer phrase.
    80	
    81	This is a general rule for the repository, not only a rule for file splits.
    82	Module names, namespace names, public declarations, theorem fields, docstrings,
    83	blueprint-facing names, issue titles, and spec documents should name the
    84	mathematical layer under discussion, not the local workflow step, paper line
    85	number, or implementation history.
    86	
    87	### Concrete examples
    88	
    89	The table below illustrates the naming norm with examples patterned on the
    90	codebase and on names seen during review.  Some entries are existing names;
    91	others are proposed names for future refactors.  The "avoid" column lists
    92	process-shaped names that encode the history of how the formalization was
    93	assembled; the "prefer" column lists mathematical names that a reader of the
    94	paper or blueprint would recognize.
    95	
    96	| Avoid (process-shaped)                        | Prefer (mathematical)                     | Rationale                                              |
    97	|:----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
    98	| `Line130`                                     | `ProjectiveConsistency`                   | Paper Lemma 5.13, not "the line-130 identity"          |
    99	| `Line169`                                     | `CompletionTransport`                     | Paper Lemma 5.16, step that transports completed data  |
   100	| `Step6`                                       | `Orthonormalization`                      | Paper Section 5, the orthonormalization construction   |
   101	| `FinalAssembly`                               | `DiagonalCompletion`                      | Paper Lemma 5.17, constructing a diagonal POVM         |
   102	| `OneShotIneq`                                 | `SelfConsistencyDataProcessing` (or existing module `Preliminaries.SelfConsistency.DataProcessing`)           | Paper's data-processing inequality for self-consistency |
   103	| `PipelineCheck`                               | `ErrorPropagationBound` (proposed)                   | The bound that propagates error through the test       |
   104	| `QxpLayerWrapper`                             | `ProjectivePOVMCompletion` (proposed)                | The construction from round-projectors to POVMs        |
   105	| `RawSpectralTruncation`                       | `SpectralTruncation`                      | The paper's spectral truncation, not an "unwrapped" version |
   106	| `AddInUStep3To5`                              | `AddInUUpperExcessMass` (proposed)                  | Paper Addendum in §U, the upper excess-mass estimate   |
   107	| `AddInUStep12`                                | `AddInUCommutationTail` (proposed)                   | Paper Addendum in §U, the commutation tail estimate    |
   108	
   109	An avoided name is acceptable only when the cited paper itself uses that
   110	phrase as the mathematical name (e.g., a lemma the paper calls "Step 2").
   111	In that case the docstring should cite the paper's phrasing.
   112	
   113	File-split PRs are a common place where this rule matters: new leaves should be
   114	named by the mathematical boundary they isolate, and any public declarations
   115	exposed by the split should be reviewed under the same standard.
   116	
   117	### Shared helpers
   118	
   119	When the same (or nearly the same) helper declaration appears in two or
   120	more chapter-local leaves, the copies should be consolidated into a single
   121	shared helper in an appropriate common module.  This avoids duplication and
   122	ensures that fixes, generalizations, or upstream replacements apply to all
   123	call sites at once.  Issue [#1145] tracks this work across the repository.
   124	
   125	Procedure:
   126	
   127	1. **Confirm equivalence.**  Compare the statement of each copy.  If the
   128	   types differ only by a chapter-specific parameterization (e.g.,
   129	   `SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι` vs `SubMeas (Point params) ι`),
   130	   parameterize the shared helper over that type via a `variable` or
   131	   explicit argument.
   132	2. **Find the right home.**  Prefer a module that is already imported by
   133	   both call sites.  Typical candidates:
   134	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/` for parameter-free operators and bounds,
   135	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Preliminaries/` for polynomial/field/character lemmas,
   136	   - The highest chapter that is a common dependency of the two sites.
   137	3. **Name mathematically.**  Give the shared helper a name that describes
   138	   what it states, not which chapter it originally came from.
   139	4. **Replace call sites.**  Delete the chapter-local copies and replace
   140	   their uses with the shared helper.  A thin wrapper is allowed only when it
   141	   preserves a paper-facing or blueprint-facing name that external readers
   142	   need to search for; such wrappers should have a docstring or compatibility
   143	   comment explaining why the alias exists.  Remove the wrapper once that
   144	   paper-facing name is no longer needed for external reference.
   145	5. **Document.**  Add a docstring to the shared helper citing the paper or
   146	   blueprint location it supports.
   147	
   148	### Legacy identifier treatment
   149	
   150	If a docstring must mention a legacy Lean identifier, cite it in backticks and
   151	describe the mathematical object in paper terminology. If an old public
   152	identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR, record the required migration
   153	in the issue, PR description, or an audit file under `audits/`.
   154	
   155	Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
   156	public name.  This is different from a documented public wrapper allowed in the
   157	shared-helper procedure above: a wrapper must preserve a paper-facing or
   158	blueprint-facing term and must say why the alias exists.
   159	
   160	## Review Checklist
   161	
   162	Reviewers should use this checklist when examining public names and
   163	documentation prose.  Flag any item that fails.
   164	
   165	- [ ] **Naming.**  Do public declaration names, namespace names, module names,
   166	      theorem field names, and docstring prose describe a mathematical object,
   167	      hypothesis, or conclusion?  Or do they encode the history of how the
   168	      formalization was assembled (paper line numbers, workflow steps,
   169	      implementation-phase labels)?
   170	- [ ] **Source alignment.**  For the mathematical content under review, does
   171	      the prose use the terminology in `references/ldt-paper/` or the
   172	      blueprint?  Are process words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`,
   173	      `raw`, `oneShot`, or `liveBlock` used as mathematical terms when the
   174	      source does not use them that way?
   175	- [ ] **Deviation documented.**  If a Lean name or representation differs from
   176	      the paper, is the deviation documented in a declaration docstring,
   177	      module docstring, blueprint paragraph, or `docs/paper-gaps/` note, in
   178	      that order of preference?
   179	- [ ] **Auxiliary lemmas.**  Are formalization-only auxiliary lemmas introduced
   180	      as such, with prose naming the nearby paper equation, theorem, or
   181	      construction they support?
   182	- [ ] **Shared helpers.**  Does the PR introduce a helper that already exists
   183	      (or near-exists) in another chapter-local leaf?  If so, has it been
   184	      consolidated into a common module with a mathematical name?
   185	- [ ] **Legacy IDs.**  If a legacy Lean identifier is mentioned, is the
   186	      mathematical object described in paper terminology?  If an old public
   187	      identifier cannot be renamed yet, is the required migration recorded in
   188	      the issue, PR description, or an audit file?
   189	- [ ] **Pass-through names.**  Does the PR add an empty pass-through
   190	      abbreviation that introduces a second public name without adding
   191	      mathematical content?  Reject it unless it is a documented compatibility
   192	      wrapper preserving paper-facing or blueprint-facing terminology.
   193	
   194	Review-fix PRs touching a surface covered by an active audit should read the
   195	relevant audit before changing names or prose.
   196

Replacing $(\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{B}''}$ by the averaged coarse-graining $\E_u \sum_{h' : g_{h'}(u) = g_h(u)} (\tau^W_{h'})_{\mathrm{B}''}$ costs at most $md/q$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree} (distinct $h \neq h'$ have distinct encodings $g_h \neq g_{h'}$, of total degree at most $md$), and by \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-6} the resulting sum equals $\E_u \sum_{a} \bra{\Delta} V_{\mathrm{A}} M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger \ot V_{\mathrm{B}} \tilde{M}^{W,\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a V_{\mathrm{B}}^\dagger \ket{\Delta}$. Exchanging $\ket{\Delta}$ for $\ket{\vartheta}$ costs $O(\delta_P^{1/4})$ by the first item, and the resulting expression $\E_u \sum_a \bra{\hat\psi} M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \ot \tilde{M}^{W,\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a \ket{\hat\psi}$ is at least $1 - O(\sqrt{\delta_P})$ by the $\simeq_{\sqrt{\delta_P}}$ relation above. Altogether the distance is $O(\delta_P^{1/4} + md/q)$; the $\mathrm{B}$-side relation is proved identically.
 \end{proof}

   293	\paragraph{Direct index sampling (candidate direction, recommended).}
   294	Define, for arbitrary $m' \ge 1$, the line-point distribution over
   295	$\F_q^{m'}$ that samples the uniform point, the uniform axis index
   296	$i \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$, and the diagonal direction with vanishing first
   297	$i-1$ coordinates, directly; define the \emph{directly indexed game} with
   298	this question distribution, whose line questions carry the index $i$ (and,

   300	$s \in \F_q$; and state the imported soundness theorem for that game

   302	else: the directly indexed game still asks for polynomials on revealed
   303	lines, has no pair questions, and weighs its branches as the present game
   304	does, so establishing form~4 carries the same two import obligations as
   305	the $\chi$-based import (Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}), now at
   306	arbitrary dimension.
   307

   309	at the level of games, not merely of question distributions, because the
   310	two games have different question alphabets: an $\mathsf{ALine}$ question
   311	of the $\chi$-based game is a pair $(u_0, s)$ and a $\mathsf{DLine}$
   312	question a triple $(u_0, s, v')$, so a strategy may select different
   313	measurements for seeds $s \ne s'$ with $\chi(s) = \chi(s')$, and equality
   314	of the induced laws of the geometric data does not by itself transport
   315	such a strategy.  The transport layer decomposes into the following
   316	obligations, none of which is carried out here.
   317	\begin{itemize}
   318	  \item \emph{Distribution lemma.}  When $m' \mid q$, the image of the
   319	  conditionally linear question distribution under the parsing map
   320	  $(u_0,s) \mapsto (u_0,\chi(s))$, $(u_0,s,v') \mapsto (u_0,\chi(s),v')$
   321	  is the direct distribution, and conditioned on the parsed question the
   322	  seed is uniform on the class $\chi^{-1}(i)$, independently of everything
   323	  else.
   324	  \item \emph{Parsing pullback.}  A strategy for the directly indexed game
   325	  composed with the parsing map is a seed-oblivious strategy for the
   326	  $\chi$-based game.  Since the win predicate depends on the question only
   327	  through the parsed data, and a seed-oblivious strategy answers
   328	  identically across each fiber --- in particular on the synchronicity
   329	  branches, where both players hold the same seed --- the value should be
   330	  preserved exactly on every branch, and projectivity is preserved.  This
   331	  is the direction the combining subtree needs.
   332	  \item \emph{Seed-fiber averaging: what it preserves and what it does
   333	  not.}  In the opposite direction, average each line measurement over its
   334	  seed fiber: attach to a direct question $(u_0,i)$, respectively
   335	  $(u_0,i,v')$, the average over uniform $s \in \chi^{-1}(i)$ of the
   336	  measurements attached to $(u_0,s)$, respectively $(u_0,s,v')$, leaving
   337	  the points measurements unchanged.  By the conditional uniformity of the
   338	  seed this preserves the value of every \emph{line-versus-point} branch
   339	  exactly: there the paired question carries no seed, so the branch value
   340	  is an average over the fiber of per-seed values, which the averaged
   341	  measurement computes.  It does \emph{not} preserve the synchronicity
   342	  branches.  There both players hold the same seed, so the $\chi$-based
   343	  branch value is the diagonal average
   344	  $\E_{s}\sum_f \langle M^{(u_0,s)}_f \ot \widetilde M^{(u_0,s)}_f
   345	  \rangle$, while the averaged strategy realizes the double average
   346	  $\E_{s,s'}\sum_f \langle M^{(u_0,s)}_f \ot \widetilde M^{(u_0,s')}_f
   347	  \rangle$ over independent seeds in the fiber; the two differ whenever
   348	  the players' measurements vary across a fiber in a correlated way (if
   349	  both apply a common seed-dependent relabelling, every diagonal term is
   350	  large and the cross terms are not), and neither quantity dominates the
   351	  other in general.  An earlier revision of this note claimed that the
   352	  averaging preserves the exact value, and with it synchronicity; that
   353	  claim was wrong and is withdrawn.  What needs proof is control of the
   354	  synchronicity branches under de-seeding.  Candidate approaches: show
   355	  that a strategy of value $1-\eps$ in the $\chi$-based game is, with
   356	  polynomial loss, close to a seed-oblivious one; or state form~4 with a
   357	  synchronicity hypothesis in the doubled-average form and re-derive it on
   358	  the tensor-code side.  Choosing and proving one of these is an open
   359	  obligation.
   360	  \item \emph{Projectivity round trip.}  The averaged strategy is a POVM
   361	  strategy even when the given one is projective, while the imported
   362	  theorem, like the present one, takes projective strategies.  The
   363	  intended round trip is: dilate the averaged strategy to a projective one

   372	  stated here as an obligation, not established.  (Alternatively, form~4
